newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka forces to protect Sinhalese hamlets.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka forces to protect Sinhalese hamlets.

text.p: Sri Lankan security forces have begun an operation to protect Sinhalese villages on the border of a large chunk of territory controlled by separatist Tamil Tiger rebels, military officials said on Thursday.
Troops and police were moving north from Vavuniya, 215 km (134 miles) north of Colombo, and from Kebitigollawa, an army-controlled town southeast of Vavuniya, a senior security official told Reuters.
"It is a combined operation by the army and police to extend our FDL (forward defended locality)," he said. "The aim of the operation is to protect the border villages."

Vavuniya is the southern entry point to a swathe of rebel-held territory in the Wanni jungle. The new military operation follows the army's capture two weeks ago of Kilinochchi, the northern gateway to the Wanni.
It was not clear if the move from Vavuniya was in preparation for an expected army push north to open the road to Kilinochchi.

No defence ministry spokesmen were immediately available for comment but the Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte said last week the military would try to reopen the highway though 70 km (45 miles) of rebel-held territory.
"That is a requirement... We want to open up all the highway and make life normal," Ratwatte said.
The Wanni separates the northern Jaffna peninsula from the rest of the mainland. It straddles the land route to Jaffna, which is now dependent on air and sea supplies.

Jaffna was seized by the military in April after being ruled for nearly a decade by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
"So far there has been no fighting with the Tigers," the security official said, referring to the operation out of Vavuniya.
Military officials said the rebels usually restrict themselves to monitoring troop movements in the early phases of an advance.
Vavuniya residents said the area was quiet.

Late last month, government troops captured Kilinochchi, the last major town under rebel control, after heavy fighting in which the military claimed that 575 rebels were killed and more than 1,000 wounded.

The army lost more than 250 soldiers in the eight-day offensive, according to official figures. The LTTE said 90 of its fighters died. With reporters banned from the war zone, no independent verification is possible.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
